model.name: claude-opus-5[1m]
model.note: Model identity is the actual runtime model of the evaluating session, taken from the session environment (claude-opus-5[1m], Opus 5 with 1M context), not the agent definition's template text, which names claude-fable-5.

issues_detected.description: is_tabular: false contradicts the record's own description, which states the modalities 'encompass tabular data, imaging data and physiological signal/waveform data', and contradicts two of its file_collections: clinical_data is CSV 'each a one-to-one mapping to the OMOP CDM tables', and the root metadata collection includes participants.tsv, a participant-level table. A defensible reading is 'not primarily tabular', but the slot is a boolean and the record asserts the opposite of what its prose and collections describe.
issues_detected.recommendation: Set is_tabular: true, since the release contains OMOP CDM CSV tables and participants.tsv, and use the description to say that tabular data is one modality among imaging and waveform data rather than the whole release

issues_detected.description: The record places accountable_organization, the principal investigator's affiliation, creators[0].affiliations[0] and the license Licensor at Washington University in St. Louis (ROR:01yc7t268), while every other source it cites points to the University of Washington: NIH RePORTER records award OT2OD032644 to the University of Washington, the reviewing IRB is the University of Washington Human Subjects Division (hsdrely@uw.edu), the BMJ Open protocol and the IRB protocol place the study there, and the RO-Crate gives 'Aaron Lee, Department of Ophthalmology, University of Washington'. The record propagates the tier-1 FAIRhub value into governance slots that carry accountability meaning.
issues_detected.recommendation: Keep the tier-1 value but record University of Washington as the co-asserted accountable organization in the governance slot itself rather than only in source_caveats, since an incorrect accountable organization misdirects access and governance enquiries

issues_detected.description: software_and_tools is absent while the record describes format-conversion pipelines in detail: Topcon .fda and FLIO .sdt converted to DICOM, Garmin .FIT converted to Open mHealth, clinical data mapped to the OMOP CDM. No tool, library or version is named for any of those conversions, and no software version appears anywhere in the record.
issues_detected.recommendation: Populate software_and_tools with the conversion and mapping tooling and their versions, and link the specific repositories under github.com/AI-READI that implement them

issues_detected.description: is_deidentified carries two mutually exclusive source claims. FAIRhub records de-identification type 'NoDeIdentification' with the explanation that no identifiers were collected so no active de-identification was necessary, while the Nature Metabolism comment describes HIPAA Safe Harbor stripping of the public set and the RO-Crate records the release as deidentified. 'Nothing was collected to remove' and 'PHI was removed under Safe Harbor' cannot both be true of the same release.
issues_detected.recommendation: State which claim governs the released bytes; the record selects HIPAA Safe Harbor as method, which is the conservative choice, but the conflict is carried forward rather than resolved

issues_detected.description: variables carries 21 entries with units and measurement techniques but no identifiers of any kind, despite the record asserting OMOP Common Data Model conformance for clinical data, RxNorm coding for the medications log, and a dqd_omop.json quality file. OMOP concept identifiers are the natural identifiers here and none appear. The record concedes that the variable detail comes from the BMJ Open protocol and healthsheet device descriptions rather than the released data dictionary, so 21 variables stand in for a release whose OMOP tables hold far more.
issues_detected.recommendation: Attach OMOP concept identifiers or LOINC codes to the laboratory and clinical variables, and state explicitly that the variable list is an illustrative subset drawn from the protocol rather than the full data dictionary

issues_detected.description: sensitive_elements_present: false and confidential_elements_present: false sit against confidentiality_level: restricted, hipaa_compliant: compliant, a license that prohibits re-identification attempts, static watermarking of released copies, and an acknowledged theoretical re-identification risk. The record does reconcile this explicitly in regulatory_restrictions.other_compliance, which says the restricted level reflects verified-ID gating and license assent rather than sensitive content, and the negative declarations follow from sex, race, ethnicity and medications having been removed before release.
issues_detected.recommendation: Retain the explicit reconciliation; consider noting that CES-D-10 depression responses and diabetes severity remain in the release, since a reuser may treat those as sensitive even where the source healthsheet does not

issues_detected.description: data_protection_impacts is absent for a multi-site human-subjects health dataset with an acknowledged theoretical re-identification risk, restricted confidentiality and NIH Genomic Data Sharing security obligations. No formal impact assessment is recorded anywhere, and the record notes the dataset 'has not undergone any formal external audit'.
issues_detected.recommendation: Record a data protection impact assessment, or state explicitly that none was conducted, so the absence is a documented finding rather than an empty slot

issues_detected.description: ethical_reviews documents IRB approval, protocol number, reliance agreements and a named ethics team, but no conflict-of-interest statement appears anywhere in the record, even though the funding block names a commercial supporter (Microsoft AI for Good Lab, which supplied cloud services) and the release is hosted on Microsoft Azure.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add a conflict-of-interest statement to ethical_reviews, addressing the commercial cloud sponsorship and hosting relationship

issues_detected.description: The dedicated download_url slot is unused and distribution_formats entries carry no access_urls, so no field in the record is a machine-readable access endpoint. Access is nonetheless fully specified in prose: page https://fairhub.io/datasets/3, the access page https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access under external_resources, and data_governance.access_review_process recording the FAIRhub access type 'PublicDownloadSelfAttestationRequired' with its three steps.
issues_detected.recommendation: Populate download_url with the FAIRhub access endpoint so automated harvesters can resolve the access route without parsing prose

issues_detected.description: source_caveats reports that the record's own sum of the nine data-type directory file counts is 356,334, nine fewer than the stated total_file_count of 356,343, and that the sum of directory sizes is 419,614 bytes short of total_size_bytes. Both discrepancies reconcile within the record itself: it declares a tenth file_collection, root_metadata, with file_count 9, which closes the file gap exactly, and those nine metadata files plausibly account for the byte gap. The caveat stops one step short of stating the reconciliation.
issues_detected.recommendation: State in source_caveats that the nine root-level metadata files close the file-count difference exactly, so the caveat reports a resolved reconciliation rather than an open discrepancy

issues_detected.description: errata, release_notes and was_derived_from are all unused. Their substance is present under other slots: change descriptions from the CHANGELOG appear in version_access.version_details, the version chain appears as related_datasets is_new_version_of entries, and source derivation appears in raw_data_sources and preprocessing_strategies. No erratum is reported for any version.
issues_detected.recommendation: State explicitly that no errata have been issued for versions 1.0.0 through 3.0.0, rather than leaving the slot empty, so absence is distinguishable from omission

issues_detected.description: The record transcribes a self-contradiction it found in the healthsheet, where one answer states the dataset 'contains data from all participants who have been enrolled during the first year of data collection' while the same document states this version covers July 19, 2023 to May 1, 2025. The record flags this in source_caveats and uses the two-year range, which is corroborated by the 2280-participant count against the 1067 of version 2.0.0.
issues_detected.recommendation: No change needed; the resolution is correct and the residual source defect is correctly attributed upstream

semantic_insights: Every internal partition in the record reconciles exactly against the participant count of 2280: the recommended splits (1576 training + 352 validation + 352 test), the race/ethnicity aggregate (380 Hispanic + 545 Asian + 519 Black + 836 White), the sex aggregate (951 male + 1329 female) and the diabetes-status groups (776 + 560 + 686 + 258). Four independent partitions summing to the stated instance count is strong evidence the composition figures were transcribed rather than approximated.

The record's own arithmetic claim in source_caveats is verifiable and correct: the nine data-type file counts sum to 356,334 and the nine total_bytes values sum to 3,815,969,360,064, exactly the figures the caveat states. A datasheet that checks its own totals and reports the residual is doing something a presence-based evaluator cannot see.

DOI 10.60775/fairhub.3 is well formed and its prefix is FAIRhub's, consistent with publisher https://fairhub.io/, page https://fairhub.io/datasets/3, the citation, and the version chain (fairhub.1, fairhub.2, fairhub.3). Identifier, landing page, publisher and citation all resolve to the same release with no drift.

All three NIH grant numbers follow valid NIH activity-code patterns and are institutionally coherent with the named sites: OT2OD032644 (Other Transaction, Office of the Director, the Common Fund Bridge2AI mechanism), P30DK035816 (NIDDK center grant) and UL1TR003096 (NCATS CTSA, matching the University of Alabama at Birmingham site). The full form 1OT2OD032644-01 with award amount and project period is recorded alongside.

HIPAA Safe Harbor is the semantically appropriate de-identification method for a multimodal clinical dataset released publicly, and the identifiers_removed list goes beyond the Safe Harbor eighteen to include sex, race/ethnicity and medications, which the record explains as stigmatization prevention rather than statutory requirement.

Temporal ordering is coherent throughout: collection 2023-07-19 to 2025-05-01, release 2025-11-17 matching both issued and the version 3.0.0 entry in distribution_dates, and the prior releases at 2024-05-03 (204 participants) and 2024-11-08 (1067 participants) forming a monotonic accrual series.

Nine ROR identifiers and one ORCID are all well formed, and ROR:01yc7t268 does denote Washington University in St. Louis, so the institutional attribution problem is a source disagreement faithfully propagated rather than a malformed or invented identifier.

The four negative declarations in the record (content_warnings_present, confidential_elements_present, sensitive_elements_present, at_risk_groups_included, each false) are all sourced to specific healthsheet answers and accompanied by explanatory detail, so they read as findings rather than empty defaults. at_risk_groups_included: false is substantively justified by the exclusion of minors, pregnant participants and prisoners.

conforms_to is expressed three ways that agree: prose naming CDS v0.1.1, WFDB, OMOP CDM, DICOM, Open mHealth, the NASA ASCII guidelines and RO-Crate 1.2-DRAFT with FAIRscape profile 0.1; a controlled conforms_to_standard enum list; and per-collection conforms_to on each of the nine data-type collections.

instances[0].label: false is consistent with the absence of labeling_strategies, annotation_analyses and machine_annotation_tools, and label_description explains the absence as a design property of a hypothesis-agnostic dataset. The empty slots are explained rather than merely empty.

Six device-specific anomaly entries name concrete failure modes tied to named instruments (Garmin Vivosmart 5 recharge gaps, Optomed Aurora undilated handheld variability, FLIO light discomfort and one-centimetre movement tolerance), which is materially more actionable than a generic data-quality paragraph.

Twenty-one collection_mechanisms entries name the specific instrument and protocol for each modality, down to scan patterns (ONH-RC, PPole-H, 12.0 x 12.0 mm OCTA at 50 kHz) and sampling rates (CGM every five minutes, Garmin every five seconds), which supports replication at the level the rubric asks for.

elements.name: Dataset Discovery and Identification
elements.description: Can a user or system discover and uniquely identify this dataset?

sub_elements.name: Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)
sub_elements.evidence: id: doi:10.60775/fairhub.3 ; doi: 10.60775/fairhub.3 ; version_access.latest_version_doi: doi:10.60775/fairhub.3 ; related_datasets target doi:10.60775/fairhub.2 and doi:10.60775/fairhub.1
sub_elements.quality_note: Well-formed DOI on the 10.XXXXX/suffix pattern with a plausible registrant prefix: 10.60775 is FAIRhub's, corroborated by publisher https://fairhub.io/ and page https://fairhub.io/datasets/3. The identifier is version-specific and the two prior versions carry their own DOIs, so the record identifies a release rather than a project. No RRID, which is not expected for a dataset of this kind.

sub_elements.name: Dataset Title and Description Completeness
sub_elements.evidence: title and name: 'Flagship Dataset of Type 2 Diabetes from the AI-READI Project'; description of roughly 1,800 characters covering the three collection sites, 2280 participants, the 2023-07-19 to 2025-05-01 window, 356,343 files at about 3.82 TB, thirteen named modalities, the tabular/imaging/waveform composition, the triple-balanced recruitment design, the 2.5-4 hour visit plus ten days of at-home monitoring, and the removal of sex, race/ethnicity and medications from the public release
sub_elements.quality_note: Far beyond the 200-character threshold and specific throughout. Every quantity it states reappears in a structured slot, and it states what is absent from the release as well as what is present, which is the harder half of a description.

sub_elements.name: Keywords or Tags for Searchability
sub_elements.evidence: keywords: Diabetes mellitus, Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, Electrocardiography, Continuous Glucose Monitoring, Retinal imaging, Eye exam
sub_elements.quality_note: Seven keywords, above the five-keyword threshold, spanning condition, method and three named modalities. Thinner than the record deserves: the OMOP data model, the wearable and environmental sensing modalities, and the Bridge2AI program are all central to the dataset and absent from the index terms. Program context is nonetheless recoverable from funders, which names the NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI program.

sub_elements.name: Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)
sub_elements.evidence: page: https://fairhub.io/datasets/3 ; file_collections: ten typed collections (cardiac_ecg, clinical_data, environment, retinal_flio, retinal_oct, retinal_octa, retinal_photography, wearable_activity_monitor, wearable_blood_glucose, root_metadata), each with id, name, path, collection_type, description, file_count, total_bytes and conforms_to; root_metadata nests nine resources entries for the individual metadata files with format and file_type
sub_elements.quality_note: Active landing page plus a genuinely hierarchical decomposition: dataset to collection to file, with sizes and standards at each level. The nested resources under root_metadata give file-level granularity for the documentation set.

sub_elements.name: Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: relationship_type is_new_version_of -> doi:10.60775/fairhub.2 (version 2.0.0, 1067 participants); relationship_type is_new_version_of -> doi:10.60775/fairhub.1 (version 1.0.0, 204 participants, pilot); relationship_type has_part -> AI-READI mini-subset version
sub_elements.quality_note: Three typed relationships with resolvable DOI targets for two of them and per-entry notes giving participant counts and release dates. The mini-subset entry carries a source_caveats explaining why it is named descriptively rather than by identifier and why containment rather than derivation was chosen, which is the right handling of an under-specified relation.

elements.name: Dataset Access and Retrieval
elements.description: Can the dataset and its associated resources be located, accessed, and downloaded?

sub_elements.name: Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined
sub_elements.evidence: license_and_use_terms.license_terms: the AI-READI Data License Agreement version 2.0 (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17555036) with storage limited to institutional servers or BAA-covered cloud, derivative and synthetic data treated as data, acknowledgement and NIH GDS security obligations, automatic termination on breach and an as-is warranty disclaimer; license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission: disease_specific_research; ip_restrictions.restrictions: title and all industrial and intellectual property rights remain with the Licensor, models may be distributed if they do not contain the data and if memorization risk has been minimized, copyright notice recorded
sub_elements.quality_note: Both halves are present and specific. The IP clause is unusually informative for a datasheet: it states what a licensee may distribute (models) and under what condition (no embedded data, memorization minimized), which is the operative question for an AI-ready release.

sub_elements.name: Regulatory Restrictions and Confidentiality Level Specified
sub_elements.evidence: regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level: restricted ; hipaa_compliant: compliant ; regulatory_restrictions list: NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy security standards, NIH Security Best Practices for Controlled-Access Data, static watermarking that must not be removed; other_compliance: study not FDA-regulated for drug or device, RO-Crate confidentiality level HL7:2N (normal), with the reason the record raised it to restricted
sub_elements.quality_note: All four sub-fields populated with named frameworks rather than labels. other_compliance does the work the semantic layer wants: it records that the source says HL7:2N normal and explains that verified-ID gating and license assent are why the record states restricted, so the divergence from the source is declared rather than silent.

sub_elements.name: Download URL or Platform Link Available
sub_elements.evidence: page: https://fairhub.io/datasets/3 ; external_resources 'FAIRhub dataset access page': https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access ; data_governance.access_review_process: verified-ID login, attestation to type 2 diabetes research only, and license assent, with FAIRhub access type 'PublicDownloadSelfAttestationRequired'; third_party_sharing.is_shared: true with the same route
sub_elements.quality_note: Platform link plus a step-by-step access procedure naming the gating mechanism and the conditions page. Scored on the rubric's 'platform access instructions' clause; the dedicated download_url slot is unused and distribution_formats carries no access_urls, so nothing in the record is a machine-readable endpoint (flagged low).

sub_elements.name: Distribution Formats and File Types Specified
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats: four entries pairing format with media_type and a description of what is distributed in it (DICOM/application/dicom for retinal imaging, CSV/text/csv for OMOP-mapped clinical data, JSON/application/json for the metadata files, Markdown/text/markdown for documentation); per-file format values MD, JSON, TXT, TSV under root_metadata.resources; per-collection conforms_to naming WFDB, OMOP CDM, DICOM, Open mHealth and the NASA ASCII guidelines
sub_elements.quality_note: Formats are named with correct MIME types and, more usefully, tied to which part of the release each covers. The waveform (WFDB) and Open mHealth outputs are described in file_collections rather than distribution_formats, so the four-entry list slightly under-reports the release's format range.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets and External Resources Linked
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: three typed entries; external_resources: ten entries with URLs including docs.aireadi.org, aireadi.org, the FAIRhub access page, zenodo.org/communities/aireadi, github.com/AI-READI, the Zenodo-archived license, the Nature Metabolism comment (doi:10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x), the BMJ Open protocol (doi:10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449) and ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06002048
sub_elements.quality_note: Ten external resources, each annotated with what it contains rather than listed bare, and the documentation entry records its own CC-BY 4.0 licence and lack of restrictions. Two peer-reviewed publications and a trial registration give the dataset independent anchors.

elements.name: Data Reuse and Interoperability
elements.description: Is sufficient information provided to reuse and integrate the dataset with others?

sub_elements.name: License Terms Allow Reuse
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: distribution_formats populated with four formats; page https://fairhub.io/datasets/3 resolves to an accessible release; third_party_sharing.is_shared: true; the license explicitly permits reuse for research and commercial purposes
sub_elements.evidence: license: AI-READI custom license v2.0 ; license_and_use_terms.license_terms: 'grants a non-exclusive, non-transferable license to download, reproduce and use the data and to create derivative works for research, commercial and non-commercial purposes'; data_use_permission: disease_specific_research; intended_uses names 'Research and commercial artificial intelligence and machine learning development'
sub_elements.quality_note: A custom rather than a standard licence, which raises the reuse cost, but the record states the permission surface precisely: reuse is granted for commercial and non-commercial research, derivative works are allowed, and the scope limit (type 2 diabetes research for the public version) is stated. source_caveats records that the FAIRhub page labels the licence 'Health Data License' while the API records 'AI-READI custom license v2.0', and says which was used.

sub_elements.name: Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: same shared-and-reusable condition as above: distribution_formats populated, accessible landing page, licence permitting reuse
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats: DICOM, CSV, JSON, Markdown with MIME types; conforms_to_standard: CDS, WFDB, OMOP_CDM, DICOM, OPEN_MHEALTH, ESDS, RO_CRATE; per-collection conforms_to values; raw_data_sources.raw_data_format records the pre-standardization forms (.xml, .csv, .fda, .sdt, .FIT, DICOM) that were converted away
sub_elements.quality_note: Every distributed format is an open or clinical-community standard, and the record distinguishes the vendor formats it started from (.fda, .sdt, .FIT) from the standard formats it ships, which is exactly the information a reuser needs. The encoding slot is unused, so character encoding for the CSV and TSV files is unstated.

sub_elements.name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: same shared-and-reusable condition as above
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to: prose naming Clinical Dataset Structure (CDS) v0.1.1 directory layout, WFDB for ECG, OMOP CDM for clinical data, DICOM for FLIO/OCT/OCTA/photography, Open mHealth for wearable and CGM, NASA ASCII File Format Guidelines for environmental sensing, and RO-Crate 1.2-DRAFT with FAIRscape profile 0.1 with one subcrate per data type; conforms_to_standard enum list; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema ; conforms_to_class: Dataset
sub_elements.quality_note: Conformance is stated at three levels that agree with each other: prose with versions, a controlled enum list, and per-collection assertions. Naming the standard version (CDS v0.1.1, RO-Crate 1.2-DRAFT, FAIRscape 0.1) rather than the bare standard is the difference between a checkable claim and a label.

sub_elements.name: Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: same shared-and-reusable condition as above
sub_elements.evidence: variables: 21 entries, each with variable_name, data_type and description, most with unit (mg/dL, logMAR, log contrast sensitivity, percent) and measurement_technique naming the instrument (Dexcom G6 sampled every 5 minutes, Garmin Vivosmart 5, LeeLab Anura, MoCA Duo on iPad, M&S Technologies EVA tester at 4 metres, Mars Perceptrix chart, University of Washington Nutrition and Obesity Research Center assays); MoCA total score carries maximum_value 30.0; best-corrected visual acuity carries quality_notes recording that Snellen variables were dropped in 3.0.0
sub_elements.quality_note: Meaningful and actionable variable-level metadata: units, instruments, ranges and a version-specific quality note. Scored 1 on that basis, but the sub-element's 'with identifiers' clause is unmet, no OMOP concept id, LOINC or other code appears on any variable despite the record asserting OMOP CDM conformance, and the record concedes the list derives from the protocol publication rather than the released data dictionary (flagged medium).

sub_elements.name: Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)
sub_elements.evidence: intended_uses: two categories with usage_notes and an example of permitted model distribution; prohibited_uses: six entries each with a prohibition_reason, covering clinical treatment decisions, re-identification and contact attempts, sharing with third-party model vendors for training even under a BAA, onward conveyance to non-licensees, reproduction beyond five figures per paper, and removal of watermarking; other_tasks records that the dataset is hypothesis-agnostic and unlabelled so users may define their own tasks
sub_elements.quality_note: The strongest use-guidance block in the record. Each prohibition states its purpose rather than just its rule, and the third-party model vendor clause is precise about what is still allowed (short-term prompting by a BAA-covered vendor) versus what is not (weight modification or training), which is the distinction a reuser will actually need.

elements.name: Ethical Use and Privacy Safeguards
elements.description: Does the dataset provide clear information about consent, privacy, and ethical oversight?

sub_elements.name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: description (E1) states the data were 'collected from individuals with and without T2DM' across three sites with study visits and at-home monitoring; keywords (E1) include 'Diabetes mellitus' and 'Eye exam'; collection_mechanisms (E8) describes recruitment and in-person participant testing; regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level: restricted and hipaa_compliant: compliant (E2) indicate governance constraints
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews: reviewing_organization 'University of Washington Institutional Review Board', protocol STUDY00016228, initial approval 20 December 2022, annual renewal within 90 days of expiration, reliance agreements with the UAB and UCSD IRBs, approval letter published with the 3.0.0 documentation, contact IRB Reliance Team at the Human Subjects Division; second entry recording ethical review of the release by four named bioethicists; human_subject_research.irb_approval and ethics_review_board repeat the protocol and board; data_governance.committee_contact names the PI with ORCID and email
sub_elements.quality_note: Protocol number, approval date, renewal cadence, reliance structure and a named contact, which is well past the threshold. source_caveats records that the RO-Crate calls the board 'Washington University IRB' while giving a University of Washington address and contact, and names the three sources that identify it as UW. data_protection_impacts is absent, which the sub-element also asks for (flagged low).

sub_elements.name: Deidentification Method Described
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: same human-subjects and governance conditions as above, evidenced from E1 description and keywords, E8 collection_mechanisms and E2 regulatory_restrictions
sub_elements.evidence: is_deidentified.method: HIPAA Safe Harbor ; identifiable_elements_present: false ; identifiers_removed: 'Protected Health Information as defined by the HIPAA Privacy Rule; participant sex; race/ethnicity; medications used'; deidentification_details records the FAIRhub 'NoDeIdentification' claim, the Safe Harbor stripping described in the Nature Metabolism comment, the RO-Crate deidentified flag, and that no formal external audit was performed but internal review checked for accidental PII
sub_elements.quality_note: A named statutory method with an explicit removed-identifier list, going beyond the Safe Harbor eighteen to sex, race/ethnicity and medications with the stated reason of preventing stigmatization. Safe Harbor is an appropriate method for a publicly released multimodal clinical dataset. The block carries two mutually exclusive source claims about whether de-identification was performed at all and selects the conservative one rather than reconciling them (flagged medium).

sub_elements.name: Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: same human-subjects and governance conditions as above
sub_elements.evidence: participant_privacy.anonymization_method: Safe Harbor removal with participants appearing only under study ID folder names; privacy_techniques: removal of sex, race/ethnicity, medications, 5-digit zip code, genetic sequencing data, past health records and traffic/accident reports, static watermarking to identify the licensee, licence terms prohibiting identification or contact, verified-ID gated access, and encrypted servers or locked rooms during collection; reidentification_risk: 'no uses resulting in unfair treatment or harm are currently anticipated but there is a theoretical risk of future re-identification'; data_linkage: files organized by participant ID so modalities can be linked; future_use_impacts records that AI algorithms could facilitate individual-level identification
sub_elements.quality_note: All four sub-fields populated, and the protections span the technical (removal, watermarking), the contractual (licence prohibitions) and the operational (encrypted storage, gated access) rather than only one. The risk statement is qualitative and forward-looking rather than a quantified assessment, but it is explicit, sourced and paired with the mitigations, and future_use_impacts names the specific mechanism of concern.

sub_elements.name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: same human-subjects and governance conditions as above
sub_elements.evidence: informed_consent.consent_obtained: true ; consent_type: written informed consent, electronically via e-consent with electronic signature in REDCap or in person at the visit; consent_documentation: signed forms, the approved University of Washington form published with the 3.0.0 documentation; consent_scope: FAIRhub consent type 'ConsentSpecifiedNotElsewhereCategorised', public version restricted to type 2 diabetes research; withdrawal_mechanism: participants could withdraw at any time, with already-shared data remaining in the dataset, communicated in the consent document; collection_consents describes the e-consent flow with unique access codes and IRB reliance using the same form; consent_revocations repeats the withdrawal terms
sub_elements.quality_note: Consent is documented across three slots that agree, and the withdrawal mechanism states the limit honestly: withdrawal stops future participation but does not retract already-distributed data, and the record notes this is disclosed in the consent form. The consent scope is tied directly to the access attestation in data_governance, so the ethics and access blocks are consistent.

sub_elements.name: Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: same human-subjects and governance conditions as above
sub_elements.evidence: at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included: false with special_protections recording that minors are excluded by the age-40 minimum, pregnancy and gestational diabetes are exclusion criteria, and the IRB protocol records that the research is not likely to have subjects who become prisoners and will not recruit or obtain data from known prisoners; participant_compensation: compensation_provided true, amount $200, type recorded as a grant-funded stipend for the study visit with parking, transit or rideshare costs covered and rideshare assistance offered to participants reporting transport barriers, plus notes on payment timing (after devices are returned, typically at least two weeks post-visit), non-proration, and the $25 transport reimbursement ceiling
sub_elements.quality_note: The negative declaration is substantively justified rather than asserted: each standard vulnerable category is addressed and excluded by a stated criterion. Compensation is documented to an unusual level of operational detail, including the transport-barrier mitigation, which is itself an equity measure consistent with the record's stated recruitment aims.

elements.name: Data Composition and Structure
elements.description: Can the dataset's structure, modality, and population be understood from metadata?

sub_elements.name: Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described
sub_elements.evidence: subpopulations: four entries (self-reported race and ethnicity, biological sex, diabetes status group, age), each with subpopulation_elements_present, identification and distribution; aggregate counts 380 Hispanic / 545 Asian / 519 Black / 836 White, 951 male / 1329 female, 776 no diabetes / 560 lifestyle-controlled / 686 oral or non-insulin controlled / 258 insulin-controlled, mean age 60.8 +/- 11.3; human_subject_research.special_populations records eligibility of adults 40 and older to a protocol maximum of 85, able to consent and to read and speak English, with pregnancy, gestational diabetes and type 1 diabetes excluded
sub_elements.quality_note: Four subpopulations with both identification and distribution, and each of the three count partitions sums exactly to the 2280 instance count. The record distinguishes correctly between variables used to balance recruitment and variables released per participant, marking subpopulation_elements_present false for race/ethnicity and sex while still reporting the aggregates, which is the honest way to describe a dataset whose balancing variables were withheld.

sub_elements.name: Number of Instances or Samples Reported
sub_elements.evidence: instances[0].counts: 2280 with instance_type 'Individual study participant'; total_file_count: 356343 ; total_size_bytes: 3815969779678 ; per-collection file_count and total_bytes for all ten file_collections; splits.split_details: training 1576, validation 352, test 352 assigned per participant in participants.tsv, in 70/15/15 proportions balanced for sex, race/ethnicity and diabetes status, with per-split mean ages
sub_elements.quality_note: Counts at three levels (participants, files, bytes) with a per-collection breakdown, and a recommended split whose parts sum exactly to the participant count. The split description explains why the balancing had to be done by the project team rather than the reuser, since the balancing variables are not released, which is a genuinely useful piece of AI-readiness documentation.

sub_elements.name: Variable-Level Metadata and Tabular Flag
sub_elements.evidence: variables: 21 entries with names, data types, units, descriptions and measurement techniques; is_tabular: false ; file_collections describe the internal structure per data type, modality and device
sub_elements.quality_note: The variable half is strong and carries units, instruments and per-variable quality notes. The flag half is wrong: is_tabular: false contradicts the record's own description ('these encompass tabular data, imaging data and physiological signal/waveform data') and the clinical_data collection of CSV files mapped one-to-one to OMOP CDM tables plus participants.tsv (flagged medium). Scored 1 because the variable metadata carries the sub-element's substance, but the boolean is a clean internal contradiction.

sub_elements.name: Data Topics or Conditions Represented
sub_elements.evidence: instances[0].data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:43 ; instance_type: 'Individual study participant' with notes listing the per-participant modalities (survey, clinical, retinal imaging, environmental sensor, continuous glucose monitor, wearable activity monitor); description names T2DM and the full modality set; subpopulations records the four diabetes severity groups; keywords name the condition and three modalities
sub_elements.quality_note: A controlled topic identifier from the Bridge2AI topic vocabulary plus prose coverage of condition and modality. The condition under study, its severity stratification and every measurement domain are all recoverable, and the instance definition states what one instance actually contains.

sub_elements.name: Data Quality Issues and Anomalies Documented
sub_elements.evidence: anomalies: six entries covering skipped or incomplete survey responses, wearable misuse and battery-driven gaps on the Garmin Vivosmart 5, imaging noise and transfer failures, undilated handheld fundus photography variability on the Optomed Aurora, FLIO acquisition discomfort and its one-centimetre movement tolerance, and manually operated devices leading to skipped modalities; sampling_strategies records non-probability sampling with the ICD-10 screening criteria (R73.09, E11.X), the wave-based recruitment with under- and oversampling, the source population and why_not_representative; missing_data_documentation gives missing_data_patterns, missing_data_causes and handling_strategy
sub_elements.quality_note: All three fields the sub-element names are populated, and the anomalies are device-specific and mechanistic rather than generic. The handling strategy is precise about who decided (site principal investigator), what was filled (values derivable from elsewhere in the record) and what was not (no modality imputation, no instances excluded at preprocessing).

elements.name: Data Provenance and Version Tracking
elements.description: Can a user determine dataset versions, update history, and provenance?

sub_elements.name: Dataset Version Number Provided
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: distribution_formats populated, page https://fairhub.io/datasets/3 accessible, licence permits reuse, third_party_sharing.is_shared true
sub_elements.evidence: version: '3.0.0' ; issued: '2025-11-17T00:00:00Z' ; version_access.latest_version_doi: doi:10.60775/fairhub.3 ; distribution_dates records 3.0.0 at 2025-11-17
sub_elements.quality_note: Semantic version tied to a DOI, a release date and a distribution-date entry that agree with each other. The version is release-specific rather than a project label.

sub_elements.name: Version Access Methods Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: same shared-and-reusable condition as above
sub_elements.evidence: version_access.versions_available: '1.0.0 (DOI 10.60775/fairhub.1, released May 3, 2024, 204 participants); 2.0.0 (DOI 10.60775/fairhub.2, released November 8, 2024, 1067 participants); 3.0.0 (DOI 10.60775/fairhub.3, released November 17, 2025, 2280 participants)'; version_details: all versions listed on the FAIRhub dataset page, each with its own documentation set at docs.aireadi.org, version 2.0.0 marked no longer accessible
sub_elements.quality_note: Every version is named with its own DOI, release date and participant count, and the record states which one is no longer retrievable. Naming a superseded version as inaccessible is more useful than listing it as if it could still be fetched.

sub_elements.name: Change Descriptions and Errata Provided
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: same shared-and-reusable condition as above
sub_elements.evidence: version_access.version_details: changes recorded in the CHANGELOG included with the release, with version 3.0.0 adding the second and third years of data collection, adding imaging devices relative to the pilot, moving from custom/ad hoc to automated plus custom processing, and dropping the Snellen visual acuity variables so only logMAR remains; variables['best-corrected visual acuity'].quality_notes repeats the Snellen removal at variable level; file_collections root_metadata.resources includes CHANGELOG.md described as recording changes between versions
sub_elements.quality_note: Four substantive changes named, one of them (the Snellen drop) propagated down to the affected variable so a reuser comparing versions finds it where it matters. The errata slot itself is unused and no erratum is reported for any version, so absence of errata is not distinguishable from omission (flagged low).

sub_elements.name: Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: same shared-and-reusable condition as above
sub_elements.evidence: updates.frequency: 'Approximately annually' ; update_details: the dataset is released as static versions and is not updated in place, new versions are released with additional instances as more participants complete the study visit, with plans for roughly annual releases and larger participant numbers since enrolment is ongoing; collection_timeframes records an anticipated completion date of 2027-01-01 and a status of 'Enrolling by invitation'
sub_elements.quality_note: Frequency plus the update model, which is the more important half: stating that versions are immutable and additive rather than revised in place tells a reuser their downloaded copy will not change underneath them. The three observed release dates (2024-05-03, 2024-11-08, 2025-11-17) are consistent with the stated cadence.

sub_elements.name: Provenance and Source Derivation Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: same shared-and-reusable condition as above
sub_elements.evidence: raw_data_sources: two entries, electronic health records screened by ICD-10 code for recruitment (used for screening only, not released) and device-native exports before standardization (.xml ECG, .csv MoCA, .fda Topcon, .sdt FLIO, .FIT Garmin, DICOM) with access_details explaining that raw data are preserved for the project duration but not shared because they are unmapped and may contain free-text PHI; preprocessing_strategies describes the mapping to OMOP and DICOM and the conversion of vendor formats; related_datasets carries the is_new_version_of chain to versions 2.0.0 and 1.0.0
sub_elements.quality_note: The derivation path from EHR screening to device capture to standardized release is traceable, and the record states which upstream artefacts exist but are withheld and why. was_derived_from and release_notes are unused, with their substance carried by raw_data_sources and version_access instead (flagged low).

elements.name: Scientific Motivation and Funding Transparency
elements.description: Does the metadata clearly state why the dataset exists and who funded it?

sub_elements.name: Motivation or Purpose for Dataset Creation
sub_elements.evidence: purposes: four entries covering enabling AI/ML insight into T2DM including salutogenic pathways, collecting and publicly sharing a multimodal AI-ready dataset balanced for severity across a diverse cohort at three sites, developing a foundational dataset agnostic to existing classification criteria for reconstructing a temporal atlas of T2DM development and reversal, and creating a blueprint other data generation projects can follow; addressing_gaps: three entries naming the lack of well-designed inclusive multimodal datasets, the lack of AI-ready diverse datasets, and a meta-epidemiological review of T2DM studies from 2000 to 2020 finding samples lacking racial and ethnic diversity
sub_elements.quality_note: Purpose and gap are stated separately and both are specific. The gap statements cite evidence (the 2000-2020 meta-epidemiological review) rather than asserting a need, and the fourth purpose, the methodological blueprint, explains why the record itself is as detailed as it is.

sub_elements.name: Primary Research Objectives or Tasks
sub_elements.evidence: tasks: pseudo-time manifold analysis to predict disease trajectories from multimodal data across the severity range from normal to insulin-dependent T2DM, and development of AI/ML models of salutogenesis and multimodal models over survey, clinical, imaging, waveform, wearable and environmental data; other_tasks: the dataset is hypothesis-agnostic and unlabelled, intended to support downstream applications beyond those planned, with no formal guidelines for user-defined tasks
sub_elements.quality_note: Named analytic methods rather than generic 'machine learning research', and the record is explicit that it provides no labels and no task guidelines, which correctly sets expectations for anyone looking for a benchmark.

sub_elements.name: Funding Sources and Mechanisms Listed
sub_elements.evidence: funders: National Institutes of Health with the award title 'Bridge2AI: Salutogenesis Data Generation Project' made through the NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI program, NIH RePORTER project number 1OT2OD032644-01, award amount 5,026,499 for fiscal year 2022 and a project period of 2022-09-01 to 2025-08-31; Research to Prevent Blindness, named in the BMJ Open funding statement; Microsoft AI for Good Lab, which supported the cloud services needed for the project
sub_elements.quality_note: Three funders with the mechanism, award title, amount and project period for the primary one, plus a non-monetary in-kind supporter identified by what it provided. source_caveats records that sources disagree on the number of NIH grants and states the tier rule applied, keeping the additional grants because they are stated as support rather than contradicted.

sub_elements.name: Grant IDs or Award Numbers Present
sub_elements.evidence: funders[0].grants: grant_number OT2OD032644 (with the full RePORTER form 1OT2OD032644-01), P30DK035816, UL1TR003096
sub_elements.quality_note: All three follow valid NIH patterns and are institutionally coherent with the record's own site list: OT2 is the Other Transaction activity code used by the Common Fund Bridge2AI program with OD for the Office of the Director, P30 is an NIDDK centre grant matching the DK institute code, and UL1TR003096 is an NCATS CTSA consistent with the University of Alabama at Birmingham site. The full grant form with year suffix is recorded alongside the base number.

sub_elements.name: Creators and Acknowledgements Documented
sub_elements.evidence: created_by: AI-READI Consortium; creators: one organizational creator with a note explaining that the DataCite metadata records a single organizational creator, a principal_investigator block giving Aaron Lee with ORCID:0000-0002-7452-1648, email and affiliation, and nine institutional affiliations each with a ROR identifier; data_collectors.notes acknowledges that team effort was supported by NIH award OT2OD032644 by percentage of effort; ethical_reviews names four bioethicists who reviewed the release
sub_elements.quality_note: Creator attribution is resolvable rather than nominal: an ORCID for the PI and nine RORs for the institutions, all well formed. The record explains why the creator list is organizational rather than a person list, citing the DataCite metadata. The PI affiliation carries the Washington University in St. Louis versus University of Washington disagreement into a governance-bearing slot (flagged medium under content accuracy).

elements.name: Technical Transparency (Data Collection and Processing)
elements.description: Can data collection and processing steps be replicated or understood?

sub_elements.name: Collection Mechanisms and Settings Described
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: acquisition_methods and collection_mechanisms are populated, and the shared-and-reusable condition holds (distribution_formats populated, accessible FAIRhub landing page, licence permitting reuse)
sub_elements.evidence: collection_mechanisms: 21 entries naming instrument and protocol per modality, including REDCap for questionnaire and clinical capture with the named instruments (CES-D-10, PAID-5, PhenX social determinants surveys, medications log with RxNorm codes), the Philips PageWriter TC30 for 12-lead ECG with body position recorded, three named oscillometric blood pressure devices, 10 g monofilament testing at three sites per foot, MoCA Duo on iPad, the M&S EVA tester at 4 metres under photopic and mesopic conditions, the Mars contrast sensitivity chart, Optomed Aurora IQ handheld fundus photography, iCare EIDON, Heidelberg Spectralis with ONH-RC, PPole-H and macular OCTA protocols, Heidelberg FLIO acquired last, Topcon Triton and Maestro2 with named scan geometries, Zeiss Cirrus 5000 Angioplex, Dexcom G6 for 10 days at 5-minute sampling with participants masked, Garmin Vivosmart 5 for 10 days at 5-second sampling, the LeeLab Anura home sensor for 10 days, and CLIA-certified local labs plus central assays; collection_timeframes gives 2023-07-19 to 2025-05-01 with the four-year project structure; data_collectors describes coordinator training, the Manual of Procedures and the certification requirement of three practice subjects
sub_elements.quality_note: The most replicable block in the record. Device make and model, scan protocol, wear duration, sampling rate, body position and masking are all recorded, and data_collectors documents the human side (training, certification, per-site data managers) that determines whether a protocol was applied consistently.

sub_elements.name: Data Acquisition Methods Listed
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: same data-collection and shared condition as above
sub_elements.evidence: acquisition_methods: two entries, directly observed measurements during the visit and at-home monitoring with was_directly_observed true, and participant-reported data via REDCap questionnaires with was_reported_by_subjects and was_validated_verified true, noting cross-referencing of entered medications against medications physically brought in or photographed; raw_data_sources: EHR screening for recruitment and device-native exports with their formats and retention terms; direct_collection.is_direct: true with the ICD-10 screening route recorded
sub_elements.quality_note: Both entries carry the provenance boolean flags, and the verification claim is backed by the specific procedure used (medication cross-referencing against physical or photographed containers) rather than asserted. The distinction between observed and self-reported data is drawn where a reuser needs it.

sub_elements.name: Preprocessing, Cleaning, Labeling, and Annotation Quality
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: external_resources (E10) references https://github.com/AI-READI, a code repository organization; purposes (E7) names creating a blueprint that future data generation projects can follow for collecting and sharing AI-ready datasets, identifying shareable methodology as a project output
sub_elements.evidence: preprocessing_strategies: two entries covering the mapping to standardized terminologies at the central project team (OMOP CDM for clinical data, DICOM for medical imaging), transformation of proprietary device exports before FAIRhub upload with .fda and .sdt converted to DICOM and .FIT converted to Open mHealth, the move from custom/ad hoc processing in 1.0.0 to automated plus custom steps, and the statement that no instances were excluded at preprocessing; cleaning_strategies: range flagging in REDCap surfaced in reports to coordinators and data managers, credibility checks against prespecified ranges, skip-pattern checks, fill of values derivable from elsewhere in a record, omission and duplication checks, all edits made only under site PI approval; missing_data_documentation.handling_strategy repeats the fill and removal rule; instances[0].label: false with label_description explaining that no labelling was performed because the dataset is hypothesis-agnostic
sub_elements.quality_note: Preprocessing and cleaning are documented as procedures with named formats, named checks and a named decision authority. labeling_strategies, annotation_analyses, machine_annotation_tools and imputation_protocols are all unused, but their absence is explained rather than silent: the dataset carries no labels by design and no modality-level imputation was performed.

sub_elements.name: Software and Tools Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: external_resources (E10) references https://github.com/AI-READI, a code repository organization; purposes (E7) names a blueprint for AI-ready data generation as a project output
sub_elements.evidence: software_and_tools absent. Tools named incidentally in other slots: REDCap (capture, range flagging, e-consent), the MoCA Duo application, the OMOP CDM Data Quality Dashboard via dqd_omop.json, https://github.com/AI-READI as an organization link, and FAIRhub hosted on Microsoft Azure. No software version appears anywhere in the record, and the format-conversion pipelines the record describes in detail (.fda and .sdt to DICOM, .FIT to Open mHealth, clinical data to OMOP CDM) name no tool, library or repository.
sub_elements.quality_note: The dedicated slot is empty and the software that produced the release is not identified. Knowing which code performed the DICOM and Open mHealth conversions and the OMOP mapping, and at which version, is the purpose of this sub-element, and none of it is recoverable. Data-capture applications named in passing under collection_mechanisms are not processing-pipeline documentation, and an organization-level GitHub link does not identify a repository (flagged medium).

sub_elements.name: External Standards and Resources Referenced
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: same shared-and-reusable condition as above
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources: ten entries with URLs, including the Nature Metabolism comment (doi:10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x), the BMJ Open protocol with full citation (Owsley C, Matthies DS, McGwin G, et al. BMJ Open 2025;15:e097449, doi:10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449), ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06002048, the Zenodo-archived licence, the docs.aireadi.org documentation with its own CC-BY 4.0 terms, the project website, the FAIRhub access page, the Zenodo community and the GitHub organization; conforms_to names seven standards with versions
sub_elements.quality_note: Two peer-reviewed publications with DOIs, a trial registration, an archived licence with its own DOI, and seven versioned standards. The documentation entry records that it is CC-BY 4.0 with no restrictions, which tells a reuser they may quote it.

elements.name: Dataset Evaluation and Limitations Disclosure
elements.description: Does the metadata communicate known risks, biases, or dataset limitations?

sub_elements.name: Known Limitations Documented
sub_elements.evidence: known_limitations: five typed entries, representativeness_limitation (urban hospital-based recruitment, no Pacific Islanders or Native Americans) with scope_impact on generalizability, coverage_limitation (not all modalities available for all participants), scope_limitation (public release excludes zip code, sex, race, ethnicity, genetic sequencing, past health records, medications, traffic and accident reports, and the raw pre-standardization data), temporal_limitation (cross-sectional with one visit, only about 10% planned to return in project year 4), and methodological_limitation (multiple imaging devices deliberately used for one measure so device and protocol differ across participants)
sub_elements.quality_note: Five limitations across distinct axes, each typed, and the first carries an explicit scope_impact naming who the derived models may fail for. The methodological limitation is unusually candid: it states a deliberate design choice that complicates analysis and explains the reason (representing the range of clinical equipment) and the mitigation (device documentation for repeatability).

sub_elements.name: Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)
sub_elements.evidence: known_biases: four entries with bias_type drawn from the controlled enum, selection_bias (volunteer bias), representation_bias (pilot phase not balanced, ongoing enrolment so periodic releases may not have achieved balance, no Pacific Islanders or Native Americans) with a mitigation_strategy of triple-balanced recruitment targets and balanced recommended splits, sampling_bias (predominantly urban hospital-based recruitment from patients with a health-system encounter) with a mitigation_strategy of uniform protocols across sites and deliberate site selection, and a second selection_bias entry on the English-language eligibility requirement creating recruitment challenges for Hispanic and Asian participants; future_use_impacts records the anticipated downstream impact including the theoretical re-identification risk and the mitigations
sub_elements.quality_note: Structured categorization using the schema's bias taxonomy, with two of four entries carrying explicit mitigation strategies. The English-language entry is the strongest disclosure in the block: it names a specific eligibility rule, the demographic groups it disadvantaged, and the reason it was adopted, which is a self-critical finding rather than a generic fairness caveat.

sub_elements.name: Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted
sub_elements.evidence: anomalies: six entries covering survey skips and incomplete responses, Garmin Vivosmart 5 misuse and battery-driven collection gaps from the 2-3 day recharge cycle, imaging noise and transfer failures, Optomed Aurora undilated handheld variability within and between patients, FLIO discomfort from prolonged light exposure with acquisition placed last in the visit and a one-centimetre movement tolerance, and manually operated devices such as the Heidelberg Spectralis leading to skipped modalities; missing_data_documentation gives the corresponding patterns, causes and handling
sub_elements.quality_note: Each anomaly names the device or modality and the physical mechanism producing it, so a reuser can predict where in the data it will appear. The FLIO entry even records the protocol consequence, that it is acquired last and so meets participants at lower compliance, which is the kind of detail that changes how an analyst treats those files.

sub_elements.name: Sensitive Content and Warnings Provided
sub_elements.evidence: content_warnings: content_warnings_present false with notes citing the healthsheet answer 'No' to whether the data might be offensive, insulting, threatening or pose a psychological safety risk; sensitive_elements: sensitive_elements_present false with sensitivity_details recording no protected health information and the removal of sex, race/ethnicity and medications; confidential_elements: confidential_elements_present false with the statement that no personally identifiable information is included
sub_elements.quality_note: All three declarations are negative but each is sourced to a specific healthsheet answer and accompanied by the reason, so they are findings rather than defaults, and they follow logically from the removals documented in is_deidentified. The declarations sit in tension with confidentiality_level: restricted, which the record reconciles explicitly in regulatory_restrictions.other_compliance by attributing the restriction to access gating rather than content (flagged low).

sub_elements.name: Ethical Review Details Including Conflicts
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews: two entries, the University of Washington IRB with protocol STUDY00016228, approval date 20 December 2022, renewal cadence, reliance agreements with UAB and UCSD, the published approval letter and a named contact, and an AI-READI ethics team entry recording review of the release by Camille Nebeker, Debra Mathews, Kadija Ferryman and Nicholas Evans with the statement that ethical, legal and social implications are considered at every stage with bioethicist guidance; source_caveats records the RO-Crate naming discrepancy for the reviewing organization
sub_elements.quality_note: Institutional and project-level ethics review are documented separately, with the ethics reviewers named individually, which is rare and checkable. No conflict-of-interest statement appears anywhere, despite a commercial in-kind funder (Microsoft AI for Good Lab) and Azure hosting (flagged low). Scored 1 because the review documentation carries substantive, verifiable detail.

elements.name: Cross-Platform and Community Integration
elements.description: Does the dataset connect to wider data ecosystems, repositories, or standards?

sub_elements.name: Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: distribution_formats populated, page https://fairhub.io/datasets/3 accessible, licence permits reuse, third_party_sharing.is_shared true
sub_elements.evidence: publisher: https://fairhub.io/ ; page: https://fairhub.io/datasets/3 ; third_party_sharing describes distribution for public use through the FAIRhub platform under DOI 10.60775/fairhub.3 ; maintainers records that the dataset is hosted on FAIRhub through Microsoft Azure; data_governance records the FAIRhub access type
sub_elements.quality_note: FAIRhub is a recognized biomedical data repository and it is the DOI registrant, the landing-page host and the access gateway, so publisher, identifier and access route are all the same platform with no indirection.

sub_elements.name: Citation and DOI for Cross-referencing
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: external_resources (E10) includes two publication references, the Nature Metabolism comment at doi:10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x and the BMJ Open protocol at doi:10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449, and the shared-and-reusable condition holds
sub_elements.evidence: citation: 'AI-READI Consortium. (2025). Flagship Dataset of Type 2 Diabetes from the AI-READI Project (3.0.0) [Data set]. FAIRhub. https://doi.org/10.60775/fairhub.3' ; doi: 10.60775/fairhub.3 ; external_resources carries the two publication DOIs and ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06002048
sub_elements.quality_note: A complete, version-pinned DataCite-style citation naming creator, year, title, version, resource type, repository and resolvable DOI. The associated publications carry their own DOIs, and the BMJ Open entry gives a full author-and-page citation, so a reuser can cite the dataset and the methods paper independently.

sub_elements.name: Community Standards or Schema Conformance
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: same shared-and-reusable condition as above
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to names Clinical Dataset Structure v0.1.1, WFDB, OMOP Common Data Model, DICOM, Open mHealth, the NASA ASCII File Format Guidelines for Earth Science Data, and RO-Crate 1.2-DRAFT with the FAIRscape profile 0.1 packaged as one subcrate per data type; conforms_to_standard: CDS, WFDB, OMOP_CDM, DICOM, OPEN_MHEALTH, ESDS, RO_CRATE; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema ; each of the nine data-type file_collections repeats its own conforms_to and conforms_to_standard
sub_elements.quality_note: Seven community standards, most with versions, asserted consistently in prose, in a controlled enum and per collection. RO-Crate packaging with a FAIRscape profile means the release is machine-readable to a second metadata ecosystem beyond this datasheet.

sub_elements.name: Outreach Materials and Documentation Links
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: same shared-and-reusable condition as above
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources: docs.aireadi.org documentation covering citation, access and training prerequisites, per-domain documentation, the Healthsheet, controlled variables and AI-readiness, shared under CC-BY 4.0; the aireadi.org project website with team and contact pages; the FAIRhub access page; zenodo.org/communities/aireadi; github.com/AI-READI; page: https://fairhub.io/datasets/3 ; maintainers gives contact routes at aireadi.org/contact and docs.aireadi.org/docs/3/contact
sub_elements.quality_note: A full documentation surface with per-version documentation sets, a community archive, a code organization and two contact routes. The record also states the documentation's own licence and that the dataset relies on it for provenance detail, which tells a reuser the datasheet is not self-sufficient and where to go.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets with Typed Relationships
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: same shared-and-reusable condition as above
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: is_new_version_of -> doi:10.60775/fairhub.2 with the version 2.0.0 release date, participant count and accessibility status; is_new_version_of -> doi:10.60775/fairhub.1 with the pilot release date and participant count; has_part -> the AI-READI mini-subset, with a source_caveats explaining that no identifier is given in the sources and that containment was chosen over derivation because the sources record only a FAIRhub parent/child relation
sub_elements.quality_note: Three relationships using controlled relationship types, two with resolvable DOI targets. The mini-subset entry is a model of restraint: it records the relation the source actually supports and states why a derivation relation was not asserted, instead of inventing a direction.

strengths: Internal arithmetic is verifiable and correct throughout. Four independent partitions of the cohort (the 70/15/15 splits, race/ethnicity, sex and diabetes-status groups) each sum exactly to the stated 2280 participants, and the record's own claim that the nine data-type directories hold 356,334 files and 3,815,969,360,064 bytes reproduces exactly from its file_collections values.

Collection is documented at a level that supports replication. Twenty-one collection_mechanisms entries name the instrument, protocol, scan geometry, wear duration and sampling rate per modality, and data_collectors documents coordinator training, the Manual of Procedures and a certification requirement of three practice subjects.

Ethics documentation is complete and internally consistent: IRB protocol number, approval date, renewal cadence and reliance agreements; e-consent and in-person consent routes with the published consent form; a withdrawal mechanism that honestly states already-distributed data are not retracted; HIPAA Safe Harbor with an explicit removed-identifier list; and compensation documented down to payment timing and the transport reimbursement ceiling.

Source disagreements are declared rather than smoothed over. Six distinct conflicts (institutional attribution, licence naming, collection start date, grant count, de-identification type, file and byte totals) are recorded in source_caveats with the tier rule applied and the chosen value named, and one transcribed source self-contradiction is attributed upstream.

Bias and limitation disclosure is specific and self-critical, including the English-language eligibility requirement named as a selection bias that disadvantaged Hispanic and Asian recruitment, and the deliberate multi-device imaging design named as a methodological limitation with its reason and mitigation.

Identifiers are resolvable and well formed across the record: a version-specific FAIRhub DOI with a chain to two prior versions, an ORCID for the principal investigator, nine ROR identifiers for institutions, three valid NIH grant numbers institutionally coherent with the named sites, and a ClinicalTrials.gov registration.
weaknesses: is_tabular: false contradicts the record's own description and its own file_collections, which include OMOP CDM tables distributed as CSV and a participants.tsv table. This is the one clean internal contradiction in the record.

software_and_tools is entirely absent. The record describes format-conversion pipelines in detail (.fda and .sdt to DICOM, .FIT to Open mHealth, clinical data to OMOP CDM) without naming a single tool, library, version or repository for any of them, so the release cannot be reproduced from the datasheet.

Governance-bearing slots carry a contested institutional attribution. accountable_organization, the PI affiliation and the licence Licensor are all Washington University in St. Louis, while the NIH award record, the reviewing IRB, the protocol publication and the RO-Crate contact address all point to the University of Washington. The conflict is caveated but the governance slots still hold one side of it.

The 21 variables carry no identifiers of any kind, no OMOP concept ids and no LOINC codes, despite the record asserting OMOP CDM conformance and shipping a data quality dashboard file, and the record concedes the list derives from the protocol publication rather than the released data dictionary.
